topline.themeS185: S184 closed the 'built but unproven' gap. S185 asks: what converts visitors into members? The site has 64 views/7d, a confirmed -46% LCP win, a functioning Oracle, 0 Oracle queries from organic visits. Three conversion levers are fully agent-buildable: (1) proactive IGNIS prompts on game/project dwell (passive readers → Oracle users), (2) 3rd-visit membership achievement nudge (repeat visitors → CTA clickers), (3) Vault Kinesis ship waveform (browsers → believers). TT-NAMED-POLICY-WAVE closes the remaining 4 first-party sinks blocking enforce-flip. ARK-DEPLOY-STRAND ships fleet protection for 30 minutes.
topline.themeS184: A 968-999 SIL brand-anchor site has no slack in features — the leverage is in proof consolidation and reliability hygiene. Close the gap between 'we built it' and 'it is proven and won't fight itself.'

founderEvidence: Goal-chain /start -> /audit -> /implement -> /closeout with explicit ask: genius-level creative thinking, personalized to THIS project's real lists/flags/blockers. Personalization anchors: TASK_BOARD 'Now (S183 runway)' open carries; S180/S181 brainstorm backlog (STATUS-PROOF-INDEX, AMBIENT-CANDIDATE-LEDGER, DR-CACHE-SMOKE); live evidence that /status/ fetches 10 /api/*.json files, field-win.json is now confirmed, and 7 workflows lack rebase. Founder-gated items (RICHER-IGNIS-LAYER decision, vaultsparked-proof.js delete, nav-sheet device verify, TT enforce-FLIP per SOUL #3) are explicitly OUT of agent scope and listed as skipped/blocked.

items.summary: The site publishes ~30 public proof JSONs, and /status/ hand-fetches 10 of them on every load with no freshness contract. Merge the proof-relevant feeds into one CI-generated /api/status-proof.json and have /status/ read a single surface.
items.why: Ten parallel fetches collapse to one RTT, and the manifest becomes a trust instrument instead of a directory of files. Self-grading is the genius layer: each embedded proof carries its source generatedAt plus a computed staleness flag, and the manifest exposes a top-level worstStale + trustScore, so /status/ can render a per-signal freshness clock (green/amber/red) that no studio site does. Info-finding outcome: a visitor or AI agent verifies the studio's entire live posture in one fetch.
items.recipe: Add scripts/build-status-proof.mjs that reads api/{uptime,field-win,ai-discovery-health,ci-status,site-health,staging-health,geo-vitals,field-verdicts,public-status,security-posture}.json, stamps each with freshnessSeconds + stale boolean (vs its own generatedAt), computes top-level worstStale/trustScore, writes api/status-proof.json (publicSafe:true, sealed-vault respected). Wire into the existing proof-generation workflow + build:check drift gate; point status/index.html at the single file with graceful per-key fallback. Add a <link rel='alternate' type='application/json' href='/api/status-proof.json'> + /agents.json cross-link so agents discover it.

Run the Trusted-Types soak probe + violation analyzer now; if the S176 default-policy bridge shows near-zero new clusters, write a dated enforce-readiness verdict so the founder-device flip is a one-line yes/no instead of a re-investigation.

Doing the probe + analysis now (the agent-attemptable 90%) leaves only the SOUL #3 device-verified enforce-flip for the founder. items.recipe: Run: node scripts/probe-tt-soak.mjs && node scripts/analyze-tt-violations.mjs. Capture the cluster count + top sinks into docs/TT_ENFORCE_READINESS_2026-06-10.md with a clear GREEN/AMBER verdict and the exact flip command. items.summary: The P0 carry blamed uptime-probe.yml, but 7 self-committing scheduled workflows push without 'git pull --rebase' first, so any of them can lose a race when a human/agent push lands in the same window. Generalize the fix to the whole class.
items.why: Avoidable CI failure noise that self-heals but erodes trust in the green dashboard and can drop a generated artifact for a cycle. Fixing the class (not the one observed instance) is the durable move. Info-finding outcome: scheduled proof refreshes stop failing on benign races.
items.recipe: In each of the 7 NO-REBASE workflows (ci-status-beacon, leaderboard-api, member-seo, og-images, rum-pull, uptime-probe, vault-narrative), add 'git pull --rebase --autostash origin main' immediately before the push step (guard with || true only where a detached/no-op state is expected). Validate every edited YAML with: npx --yes js-yaml <file> >/dev/null (per the validate-workflow-yaml memory) before committing.

items.summary: The Worker disaster-recovery cache (serves stale HTML on a double-5xx, emits X-VS-Disaster-Recovery: stale) is asserted in worker-lib.mjs but never exercised by a test. Add a smoke test that forces the double-5xx path and asserts the DR header.
items.why: An untested failover is a hope, not a guarantee — the only time you find out it's broken is during the outage it was built for. A deterministic test promotes the DR layer from 'assumed' to 'proven' and guards against silent regression. Info-finding outcome: CI proves the site degrades gracefully instead of hanging.
items.recipe: Add tests/dr-cache.spec.js (Node/worker-harness style matching existing cloudflare tests) that stubs originFetch to return two consecutive 5xx, invokes the worker-lib handler, and asserts response is the cached body + header X-VS-Disaster-Recovery: stale. Wire into the test suite run by build:check. Reference: cloudflare/worker-lib.mjs (X-VS-Disaster-Recovery).

items.summary: Ambient-bundle split decisions live in a volatile .cache/ambient-split-candidates.json with no committed rationale. Promote it to a reason-coded ledger (sitewide / route-scoped / hook-scoped / keep) so future split waves are data-driven, not re-derived.
items.why: Each ambient-split wave currently re-litigates which engines belong in the cold path; a committed ledger with reason codes makes the next wave a lookup, not an investigation, and documents why each engine is where it is. Info-finding outcome: the cold-path budget has an auditable provenance trail.
items.recipe: Add scripts/build-ambient-ledger.mjs that reads the candidate cache + current ambient block composition and writes docs/AMBIENT_LEDGER.md (or context/ambient-ledger.json) with {asset, placement, reasonCode, lastReviewed}. Seed reason codes from the existing S147/S180 split decisions. Optionally gate drift in build:check.

itemsS185.conversionOutcome: Passive readers convert to Oracle question-askers; detectable via palette telemetry (open from contextual vs Cmd+K).
itemsS185.summary: Visitors spend 20+ seconds on game/project cards and then leave without ever asking IGNIS the obvious question. Surface a dismissible contextual prompt with a pre-seeded query after 20s dwell — zero extra API cost, reuses the existing edge fn.
itemsS185.why: A visitor reading the Football GM card for 20s is already curious — they just need a nudge. 'What makes Football GM different from Madden?' is the exact question they're thinking. Meeting them at curiosity-peak converts passive browsing into an Oracle interaction, which is the highest-intent engagement signal on the site.
itemsS185.recipe: Add `data-ignis-hint` to `.game-card` + `.project-card` during `propagate-nav.mjs`; in `ignis-answer-engine.js` add IntersectionObserver + 20s timer → inject `.vs-ignis-hint` strip with pre-seeded query using a named TT policy. Dismiss stores to sessionStorage. Guard with `body[data-vs-signed-in]` to avoid redundancy for members.

itemsS185.conversionOutcome: 3rd+ visit renders membership nudge; /membership/ CTA click measurable via RUM route tracking.
itemsS185.summary: The returning-visitor-digest tracks visit count and shows ships — but never converts that momentum into a membership ask. A visitor returning for the third time has already self-qualified as interested; show them an earned CTA using the rank vocabulary they've seen.
itemsS185.why: Cold CTAs perform poorly because they ask before earning trust. A visitor who returns three times has already decided to come back — they just need a specific, vocabulary-coherent ask: 'Vault Rank Iron Sentinel members get early game access. You've visited 3 times — ready?' This is the rank system doing its job.
itemsS185.recipe: In `assets/returning-visitor-digest.js` after `visitCount > 2` branch: append a 'membership nudge' row below the ships strip with entry rank + one concrete benefit from `api/public-intelligence.json`. Guard with `body:not([data-vs-signed-in])`. Link to `/membership/`. Keep same honest-dark pattern (never show without a real benefit to name).

itemsS185.conversionOutcome: Scroll depth and dwell on /studio-pulse/ increase; anonymous visitors who see active ship activity convert to signed-in members at higher rate.
itemsS185.summary: The studio ships constantly — but visitors see a static session list, not a felt sense of motion. An animated waveform on /studio-pulse/ that peaks at each ship event in the last 30 days turns the commit log into evidence of aliveness. No game studio does anything like it.
itemsS185.why: The biggest differentiator between a live studio and an abandoned project page is felt velocity. A CSS waveform 'breathing' at the ship cadence lets a visitor's eye confirm the studio is active before they read a single word. This is trust in a shape.
itemsS185.recipe: New `assets/vault-kinesis.js`: load `api/commit-map.json` + `api/ship-receipts.json`; build a 30-bucket daily timeline; render as an SVG waveform with CSS animation peaking proportionally to recent velocity; mount via ambient-loader on `/studio-pulse/` predicate. Respects `prefers-reduced-motion` (no animation, static bars).

itemsS185.conversionOutcome: TT violations drop from 148/30d toward near-zero; enforce-flip becomes viable, eliminating an entire class of DOM-injection attack surface.
itemsS185.summary: Four first-party sinks block the TT enforce-flip: journal/dispatches:364 (30×, recurring), home-idle-loader.js:16, schema-injector.js:23, ambient.shell:337/367. The dispatches sink is highest-volume AND a regression from S174 — the dispatch template rebuild is reintroducing an innerHTML path. Named policies + a lint gate make this fix structural.
itemsS185.why: The default-policy bridge buys time but doesn't close the loop. Each named-policy migration is one innerHTML call wrapped in a policy object — 30 minutes per sink. The dispatch sink's recurrence means the fix must also gate the template generator, not just the runtime. Same 'fix at the ledger level' pattern that closed the style-extractor class.
itemsS185.recipe: 1) `grep -n 'innerHTML\|insertAdjacentHTML' journal/dispatches/ assets/home-idle-loader.js assets/schema-injector.js` — wrap each with `trustedTypes.createPolicy('vs-[name]-policy', {createHTML: s => s}).createHTML(...)`. 2) Add `check-tt-named-policy.mjs` gate to `build:check`. 3) Ship football-gm sinks as Ark cargo `pattern-share` to football-gm slug (CANON-018, not website-fixable).

itemsS185.conversionOutcome: Every CF-Pages sibling repo that drains this cargo gains silent-deploy-strand protection; prevents the exact 'confirmed but never deployed' failure class.
itemsS185.summary: The [skip ci] tip strand silently broke deploy→prod for multiple sessions before root-cause. Other CF-Pages repos almost certainly have the same autopilot closeout pattern. Broadcasting the fix is 30 minutes with fleet-wide blast radius.
itemsS185.why: The Ark was built precisely for this: a proven fix that took multiple session-cycles to find, now preventable in 10 minutes for every sibling. 30 minutes of effort × ~8 sibling repos = a pattern that never bites the fleet again.
itemsS185.recipe: `node scripts/ark.mjs ship --type pattern-share --to '*' --payload '{"pattern":"cf-pages-skip-ci-tip-strand","context":"CF Pages skips [skip ci] tips; closeout autopilot reconcile commits strand the substantive deploy","solution":"check-deploy-tip.mjs guard before push; empty non-skip-ci commit when tip is [skip ci]","tags":["cloudflare-pages","ci","deploy","closeout"]}'`

itemsS185.conversionOutcome: Repeat Oracle queries return <50ms vs ~800ms; encourages multi-query exploration which correlates with higher intent and reduced Supabase edge fn token spend.
itemsS185.summary: The command-palette makes a fresh Supabase edge fn call on every Cmd+Enter, including repeat queries from exploratory users. A localStorage cache (15-min TTL, keyed by normalized query hash) eliminates redundant tokens and makes the palette feel instant on revisit.
itemsS185.why: An exploratory visitor who rephrases the same question twice currently pays 800ms twice. A cache that returns 'stale from 4 minutes ago' instantly trains them that IGNIS is fast, not slow — and the same query never costs tokens twice in the same session.
itemsS185.recipe: In `assets/command-palette.js` `aiSearch()`: compute `hash = btoa(query.toLowerCase().trim()).slice(0,16)`; check `localStorage.getItem('vs_ignis_q_' + hash)` for `{ts, result}` — if present and `Date.now()-ts < 900000`, return immediately with stale indicator. On miss, fetch + cache. Max 20 entries; evict LRU on overflow.

itemsS185.conversionOutcome: AI agents and automated trust-checkers discover /api/status-proof.json without scraping /status/; improves studio trust legibility for AI-driven referrals.
itemsS185.summary: The /api/status-proof.json manifest grades the studio's infrastructure on 10 dimensions with freshness scores — the most machine-legible trust surface the studio has. But it's only reachable by humans. One cross-link in agents.json + llms.txt closes the discovery gap.
itemsS185.why: An AI agent crawling the site will find agents.json, trust its declarations, and then want to verify operational health. Right now it has to guess or scrape. A declared statusProof field makes the trust story legible in one step — and that's the kind of thing that differentiates VaultSpark in AI-to-AI referral chains.
itemsS185.recipe: In `scripts/build-agents-json.mjs`, add `"statusProof": "/api/status-proof.json"` to the `discovery` object. In the llms.txt template/builder, append `## Operational Trust\n/api/status-proof.json — self-grading 10-dimension proof manifest with freshness timestamps.`

itemsS185.conversionOutcome: Visitors see 'Studio Pulse' everywhere — coherent vocabulary reduces exit-from-confusion before exploring the page.
itemsS185.summary: Any remaining 'Forge Window' references in generated copy create vocabulary fragmentation. Propagation takes minutes via propagate-nav.mjs and a build:check grep gate prevents regression.
itemsS185.why: A visitor who sees 'Forge Window' in one place and 'Studio Pulse' in another infers they're different things, then doubts which one they found. Vocabulary coherence is the simplest form of trust.
itemsS185.recipe: Run `grep -rn 'Forge Window' --include='*.html' --include='*.js' --include='*.mjs'`; update `propagate-nav.mjs` copy entries; add `check-vocabulary-consistency.mjs` gate (grep for 'Forge Window' in public-facing HTML → fail on match) wired into `build:check`.

itemsS185.conversionOutcome: Feature bundle reduces 52KB→~42KB; cold-cache FCP improves for first-time visitors not landing on a split-candidate target route.
itemsS185.summary: The ambient ledger already identified 4 split-candidates with reason codes. The pattern is proven (Wave 2: −23%; Wave 3: −22%); the 4 remaining candidates can be moved with the same predicate-guard template.
itemsS185.why: Every cold-cache visit pays for the feature bundle. Each wave of predicate-gating moves cost from every visitor to only the subset who need it. The ledger shows exactly which 4 assets are eligible — no re-investigation needed.
itemsS185.recipe: Read `.cache/ambient-ledger.json` `split-candidate` entries; for each, add a predicate function to `ambient-loader.js` mirroring the mount guard in the script; move it from the unconditional list to the predicated list; run `check-ambient-placement.mjs` + `build:check`. Shell-rotate if any ambient source moves.

itemsS185.conversionOutcome: Oracle answers improve for real visitor question categories; query-to-satisfied-exit rate improves (no immediate bounce after Oracle).
itemsS185.summary: api/oracle-queries.json records real visitor queries but they're never fed back into the search index. Clustering them into 5 intent categories (gaming, membership, dev, investor, lore) and writing to api/oracle-insights.json lets ignis-search-index bias toward real patterns.
itemsS185.why: This is the only AI improvement that gets cheaper over time — more queries = better bias = less waste per call. And it requires zero LLM calls: pure keyword clustering over the existing committed query log.
itemsS185.recipe: New `scripts/build-oracle-query-clusters.mjs`: read `api/oracle-queries.json`, bucket into 5 categories via keyword matching, write top-3 per category to `api/oracle-insights.json`; update `build-ignis-search-index.mjs` to consume this as a ranking-weight overlay. Wire into `npm run build`.

itemsS185.conversionOutcome: Non-US LCP verdict either confirms global win or surfaces a CDN routing gap; either outcome improves global visitor experience.
itemsS185.summary: GB has 3 RUM samples — below threshold. At current UK traffic rates this stays indefinitely below minimum. Extending probe-uptime.mjs to also measure TTFB from a EU colo provides synthetic signal for cross-checking the origin migration win globally.
itemsS185.why: The US win is confirmed (-46% LCP) but 93% of the internet is not US. 'Watch and wait' is fine when samples accrue in days, but at current UK traffic rates it could be weeks. A synthetic EU probe closes the gap without waiting.
itemsS185.recipe: In `scripts/probe-uptime.mjs`, add a secondary probe leg to a CF EU colo (using `fetch` with a Cloudflare-colocation-specific URL or header-based detection); write results to `api/geo-vitals.json` as a `synthetic` bucket separate from real-user data. `build-geo-vitals.mjs` surfaces `syntheticEuTtfbP75` clearly labeled.

itemsS185.conversionOutcome: Anonymous visitors who reach stage 3 (3 Oracle queries) click /membership/ CTA at measurably higher rate vs. cold CTA control.
itemsS185.summary: A 5-stage localStorage progression — anonymous → Shadow Member → Intelligence clearance after 3 queries → locked benefit preview on return → signup with personalized rank preview — makes visitors feel they're already progressing. Zero backend cost; SOUL #2 compliance (no membership features until auth, all stages cosmetic/aspirational).
itemsS185.why: Cold CTAs ask before earning trust. Progression hooks let visitors discover what they're missing through their own behavior. The 9-tier rank system was purpose-built for this; it just needs an anonymous on-ramp to show its value before the first password.
itemsS185.recipe: New `assets/vault-progression.js`: manage `vs_progression_stage` in localStorage (0–4); trigger stage advance on behavioral events (3 page loads, 3 palette queries, return visit, preview hover); render a distinct ambient badge in the nav. Each stage shows a different teaser. Gated by `body:not([data-vs-signed-in])`.
